Description:
Role Overview
The Assistant Professor - General Surgery is an early-career faculty and clinical role combining undergraduate teaching, supervised postgraduate training, patient care, operative practice, academic contribution, and departmental service. The position reports to the Head of the Department of Surgery and supports safe, evidence-informed surgical care across outpatient, inpatient, emergency, and operation-theatre settings. A NABH-accredited tertiary teaching hospital integrating patient care, undergraduate education, postgraduate training, research, and multidisciplinary surgical services. The appointee is expected to model professional conduct, strengthen learner competence, contribute to service continuity, and accept responsibilities assigned within the scope of General Surgery.

Key Responsibilities
Deliver structured undergraduate lectures, tutorials, demonstrations, and case-based sessions aligned with the approved curriculum and departmental teaching plan.
Conduct undergraduate clinical classes using bedside, outpatient, ward, skills-laboratory, and discussion-based methods while protecting patient dignity and consent.
Assess learner progress through appropriate formative and summative activities, provide actionable feedback, and maintain accurate academic records as assigned.
Manage scheduled outpatient consultations by obtaining focused histories, examining patients, planning investigations, documenting decisions, and arranging follow-up or admission when indicated.
Evaluate inpatients admitted under the assigned unit, review clinical progress, coordinate treatment plans, and respond promptly to referrals from other departments.
Attend emergency surgical patients during rostered on-call periods, support timely stabilization and escalation, and document assessment, consent, treatment, and handover decisions.
Perform and assist surgical procedures within demonstrated competence, granted privileges, institutional protocols, and the supervision arrangements applicable to the case.
Attend assigned operation-theatre schedules, complete preoperative preparation, participate in operative decision-making, and ensure appropriate postoperative review and continuity of care.
Supervise postgraduate trainees in theatre and clinical areas, matching responsibility to competence while maintaining patient safety and accountable faculty oversight.
Coordinate multidisciplinary care with anaesthesia, critical care, radiology, pathology, nursing, rehabilitation, and other specialties when patient needs require collaborative management.
Maintain complete, timely, and confidential clinical documentation and follow applicable requirements for infection prevention, surgical safety, quality assurance, ethics, and incident reporting.
Cover the defined duties of other Assistant Professors during approved leave, subject to departmental rosters, clinical competence, workload, and safe service arrangements.
Develop accurate public-education articles on surgical health topics for approved media channels, using evidence-based language and appropriate institutional review processes.
Undertake other academic, clinical, administrative, research, quality-improvement, and departmental responsibilities assigned by the Head of Surgery within the role's lawful scope.

Required Qualifications
MBBS from a medical institution recognised for registration and practice in India.
MS in General Surgery or DNB in General Surgery from a recognised awarding body, with equivalence documentation where applicable.
Eligibility for appointment as Assistant Professor under the Medical Institutions (Qualifications of Faculty) Regulations, 2025 and subsequent applicable NMC directions.
Current, valid registration with the National Medical Commission or the relevant State Medical Council, with no unresolved restriction affecting the proposed duties.
Documentary evidence supporting qualifications, registration, experience, appointments, relieving dates, and the specific NMC eligibility pathway claimed.

Required Experience
Minimum experience: The candidate must meet an applicable NMC Assistant Professor pathway. Under the standard pathway, this includes 1 year as Senior Resident in General Surgery in a recognised medical institution after the relevant postgraduate qualification. Candidates relying on another permitted pathway must provide complete evidence satisfying the conditions attached to that pathway; institutional verification remains mandatory.
Relevant experience must demonstrate active General Surgery work across outpatient assessment, inpatient management, interdepartmental referrals, emergency or on-call coverage, operative participation, postoperative care, clinical documentation, and undergraduate teaching. Experience should be supported by verifiable appointment, tenure, duty, and experience records rather than self-description alone.
Preferred experience: Documented clinical teaching, resident supervision, research, audit, patient-safety work, or quality improvement beyond the regulatory minimum will strengthen suitability but does not replace mandatory NMC eligibility.

Technical and Functional Skills
General surgical assessment, differential diagnosis, risk stratification, investigation planning, perioperative decision-making, and evidence-informed patient management.
Outpatient, inpatient, referral, emergency, on-call, preoperative, intraoperative, postoperative, and discharge-care workflows relevant to General Surgery.
Operative assisting and operating capability appropriate to training, recent experience, documented competence, supervision level, and institutional clinical privileges.
Safe surgery practices covering consent, identification, checklist compliance, antibiotic stewardship, blood-product awareness, infection prevention, and structured handover.
Undergraduate curriculum delivery, clinical demonstration, bedside teaching, case discussion, learner assessment, feedback, and maintenance of academic documentation.
Postgraduate supervision that calibrates delegation to trainee competence and preserves direct faculty accountability for patient care and escalation.
Interpretation and application of relevant clinical records, laboratory results, imaging reports, pathology findings, and multidisciplinary recommendations.
Use of electronic or computerised medical records, presentation software, online academic resources, and routine departmental communication systems.
Clinical audit, research ethics, literature appraisal, scientific writing, public health communication, and preparation of accurate surgical education material.
Working knowledge of NMC faculty eligibility, medical education expectations, institutional policies, ethical practice, confidentiality, and professional documentation.

Soft Skills and Behavioural Competencies
Clear, respectful communication with patients, families, learners, colleagues, and multidisciplinary teams, including difficult conversations and safe handovers.
Professional judgement, integrity, confidentiality, accountability, and willingness to disclose uncertainty or seek senior support when required.
Calm prioritisation during emergencies, changing theatre demands, competing clinical responsibilities, and on-call escalation.
Patient-centred empathy and culturally respectful behaviour without compromising clinical standards, consent, safety, or documentation.
Teaching presence that encourages questions, corrects errors constructively, and differentiates supervision according to learner competence.
Reliability, punctuality, collegiality, adaptability, and readiness to provide approved cross-coverage within safe workload limits.
Commitment to continuous learning, reflective practice, audit, research, quality improvement, and feedback-driven professional development.

Preferred or Value-Added Qualifications
Completed recognised training in medical education, biomedical research, research methodology, clinical audit, or evidence-based medicine.
Peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, surgical audits, teaching innovations, or verified contributions to public surgical education.
Experience in a tertiary-care teaching environment managing diverse elective and emergency General Surgery presentations.
Demonstrated participation in surgical safety, morbidity and mortality review, infection prevention, antimicrobial stewardship, or accreditation activities.
Readiness to complete faculty-development or research courses within the timelines required by the applicable NMC pathway or institutional policy.

Professional Tenure and Background
An appropriate background includes a documented progression from MBBS and recognised postgraduate General Surgery training into Senior Residency or another valid NMC pathway, followed by increasingly accountable clinical, teaching, and operative duties. Appointment and experience records should clearly identify institution, department, designation, dates, employment status, bed-strength or recognition evidence when relevant, and responsibilities supporting eligibility.
Experience in recognised medical institutions, teaching hospitals, or appropriately documented government-hospital pathways is valued because it supports verifiable exposure to structured education, governance, multidisciplinary care, and clinical accountability. Selection will be based on regulatory eligibility, evidence of competence, role relevance, and verified accomplishments rather than employer prestige alone.

Compensation and Benefits
The selected candidate will receive competitive, role-aligned remuneration and benefits in accordance with institutional policy, verified credentials, experience, responsibilities, and the final terms of appointment. Exact financial terms will be communicated through the formal selection process.

Application Instructions
Submit an updated resume with the role title, MBBS and postgraduate qualification details, registration status, complete employment chronology, Senior Residency or alternate-pathway evidence, teaching and operative experience, publications or audits, and current contact details. Candidates may apply through email, LinkedIn message, or WhatsApp using the contact information stated in the LinkedIn outreach post. Shortlisting and appointment remain subject to document verification, NMC eligibility review, reference checks, and institutional selection requirements.

Role Overview
The Assistant Professor - Forensic Medicine & Toxicology is a full-time academic faculty position responsible for teaching, assessment, medico-legal practice, research, and departmental service. The role supports undergraduate MBBS students, postgraduate medical students, and interns through competency-based instruction, supervised practical learning, and reliable academic evaluation. Reporting to the Head of Department, the incumbent will contribute to autopsy services, expert opinions, court duties, curriculum delivery, and institutional responsibilities. The position requires sound professional judgment, ethical conduct, accurate documentation, and the ability to connect forensic principles with clinically and legally relevant practice.

Key Responsibilities
a. Deliver structured lectures, practical demonstrations, tutorials, seminars, and supervised training for MBBS, postgraduate medical students, and interns.
b. Design teaching schedules, lesson plans, learning resources, competency maps, and assessment activities aligned with the approved curriculum and applicable NMC standards.
c. Conduct medico-legal autopsies and related examinations within authorized scope, maintaining accuracy, dignity, biosafety, evidence integrity, and complete contemporaneous records.
d. Prepare clear post-mortem reports, medico-legal opinions, certificates, and advisory inputs for authorized public authorities when formally required.
e. Attend court proceedings, present impartial medical evidence, explain findings within professional competence, and maintain secure case documentation.
f. Develop and administer internal assessments, practical examinations, viva voce evaluations, university examinations, feedback processes, and remediation plans.
g. Guide student research, dissertations, presentations, and scholarly projects while ensuring ethical approval, methodological rigor, and responsible research conduct.
h. Undertake independent and collaborative research, contribute to publications, and participate in seminars, webinars, conferences, workshops, and continuing professional development.
i. Maintain the departmental museum, specimens, displays, registers, inventories, teaching aids, and associated documentation in accordance with safety and ethical requirements.
j. Coordinate assigned departmental activities, academic records, accreditation evidence, timetables, examination duties, and other responsibilities delegated by authorized institutional leadership.
k. Complete or maintain applicable faculty-development requirements, including biomedical research and medical-education training prescribed by current regulations or institutional policy.
l. Uphold confidentiality, impartiality, chain-of-custody controls, professional ethics, infection prevention, quality systems, and respectful interprofessional collaboration.

Required Qualifications
MBBS and MD/DNB in Forensic Medicine and Toxicology from institutions and programmes recognized for faculty eligibility under current National Medical Commission requirements are mandatory. The candidate must hold active registration with the relevant State Medical Council or NMC-recognized registration authority, as applicable. DNB candidates must satisfy any additional teaching-equivalence or Senior Residency requirement applicable to the awarding institution and prevailing regulations. All degrees, registrations, experience records, and equivalence documents must be valid and independently verifiable.

Required Experience
The minimum requirement is one year of qualifying post-PG experience in the concerned subject, normally as a Senior Resident in a recognized medical institution, or another pathway expressly recognized under current NMC regulations. Recognized alternatives may include eligible postgraduate Tutor experience, qualifying Armed Forces experience, or qualifying government-hospital service, subject to documentary verification and the conditions prescribed for that pathway. Candidates should demonstrate relevant exposure to medical teaching, medico-legal autopsy work, report preparation, court processes, and departmental administration. A total of 2-4 years of relevant post-PG teaching or medico-legal experience is preferred.

Technical and Functional Skills
The role requires working knowledge of forensic pathology, toxicology, thanatology, medical jurisprudence, autopsy technique, injury interpretation, preservation and dispatch of samples, chain of custody, medico-legal documentation, expert opinion, and courtroom testimony. The candidate should be able to apply competency-based medical education, curriculum planning, student assessment, feedback, research methodology, ethics, scientific writing, and basic biostatistical interpretation. Proficiency with presentation software, digital learning platforms, academic records, literature databases, and routine office applications is expected.

Soft Skills and Behavioural Competencies
Essential behaviours include integrity, impartiality, discretion, attention to detail, calm decision-making, clear written and oral communication, and respect for legal and ethical boundaries. The incumbent must teach complex or sensitive material with maturity, collaborate effectively with students, clinicians, administrators, laboratory teams, law-enforcement personnel, and judicial stakeholders, and manage competing academic and medico-legal priorities. Reliability, empathy, cultural sensitivity, accountability, and commitment to continuous learning are central to success.

Preferred or Value-Added Qualifications
Preference may be given to candidates who have completed the Basic Course in Biomedical Research and relevant medical-education or faculty-development training; have verifiable publications, conference presentations, or student-guidance experience; and have handled court testimony, curriculum development, university examinations, accreditation documentation, or museum curation. Training in research ethics, good clinical practice, educational technology, simulation, or quality improvement will strengthen the candidature.

Professional Tenure and Background
An appropriate career path includes MBBS, recognized postgraduate specialization in Forensic Medicine and Toxicology, and qualifying post-PG experience. The preferred profile offers 2-4 years of relevant exposure in recognized medical colleges, teaching hospitals, authorized medico-legal services, or other institutions accepted under current NMC pathways. Progressively responsible teaching, autopsy, court, research, assessment, and departmental assignments are valued.

Compensation and Benefits
The appointment offers competitive, role-aligned compensation and faculty benefits governed by institutional policy, qualifications, verified experience, and internal parity. Applicable benefits and any professional-development, conference, or research support will be communicated during the selection process.

Application Instructions
Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, qualification certificates, registration proof, eligibility and experience records, publication list, and verifiable evidence of teaching, autopsy, court, research, and academic administration. Applications must be accurate and complete; eligibility and experience will be verified.

The Associate Professor of General Surgery is a senior academic-clinical faculty position responsible for undergraduate and postgraduate teaching, supervised surgical training, patient care, assessment, research, and departmental service. The role reports to the Head of Department or Professor and works across classrooms, bedside clinics, outpatient and inpatient services, emergency duty, and operation-theatre schedules. This is an on-site appointment in Gangtok, Sikkim. The appointee will strengthen learner competence, safe surgical practice, clinical governance, and patient satisfaction through disciplined teaching and continuous improvement. The employer is a confidential tertiary teaching hospital integrating patient care, education, clinical training, and research.

Key Responsibilities
Deliver structured lectures, tutorials, demonstrations, and clinical classes for MBBS students in alignment with the approved curriculum.
Conduct postgraduate seminars, case discussions, journal clubs, clinical meetings, and bedside teaching for General Surgery trainees.
Mentor interns, residents, and postgraduate students in clinical reasoning, procedural competence, professional conduct, documentation, and patient communication.
Plan and implement competency-based teaching, formative feedback, workplace-based assessment, and remedial support for learners requiring improvement.
Serve as an internal or external examiner when appointed and contribute to fair, confidential, and evidence-based undergraduate and postgraduate assessment.
Attend scheduled outpatient clinics, evaluate new and follow-up patients, establish management plans, and maintain timely clinical records.
Manage inpatients admitted under the assigned unit and respond appropriately to interdepartmental referrals requiring surgical evaluation.
Provide emergency surgical assessment and treatment during allocated on-call duties, escalating complex cases through established clinical pathways.

MBBS from an institution recognised under applicable Indian medical-education requirements.

Documented eligibility for appointment as Associate Professor in General Surgery under current National Medical Commission requirements.

Outpatient, inpatient, referral, critical-care interface, discharge, follow-up, and continuity-of-care workflows.
Competency-based medical education, curriculum delivery, bedside teaching, assessment design, feedback, and remediation.
Clinical documentation, informed consent, medical records, patient confidentiality, medico-legal awareness, and ethical practice.
Research methods, literature appraisal, clinical audit, manuscript development, publication ethics, and academic presentations.
Quality improvement, infection prevention, antibiotic stewardship, morbidity-and-mortality review, and patient-safety systems.

Clear teaching, listening, feedback, counselling, accountability, and interdisciplinary communication.
Calm, respectful, ethical leadership with sound judgement, adaptability, empathy, and appropriate escalation.

Laparoscopic or minimally invasive surgical expertise, plus additional achievement in trauma, critical care, education, simulation, research, quality, digital systems, or mentoring.

Professor - Department of Ophthalmology - Job Description

Department: Ophthalmology.

Employment Type: Full-time faculty position.

Role Overview
The Professor of Ophthalmology is a senior faculty position at a leading super speciality teaching hospital and medical college run by a renowned university, uniting patient care, teaching and research. The role combines evidence-based general and subspeciality eye care with delivery of the Competency Based Medical Education (CBME) curriculum prescribed by the National Medical Commission (NMC). The Professor mentors junior faculty, residents and interns, guides postgraduate theses, and strengthens the department's research output and academic standing. The position reports to the Head of the Department of Ophthalmology, or to the Dean and Medical Superintendent where the Professor heads the department, as per institutional structure.
Work Mode

Work mode: Work from office, on-campus at the teaching hospital, with working days and on-campus attendance as per teaching hospital and NMC norms, including NMC-mandated faculty attendance recording. No routine travel requirement has been specified; occasional academic, examiner or community outreach duties may be assigned as per institutional needs.

Key Responsibilities
Deliver undergraduate (MBBS) Ophthalmology teaching through lectures, small-group sessions, clinical postings and skills-lab training as per the NMC CBME curriculum, including AETCOM components.
Lead postgraduate training of MS Ophthalmology residents through seminars, journal clubs, case presentations, wet-lab sessions and supervised surgical training, where the programme is offered.
Guide and co-guide postgraduate theses, ensuring sound methodology, ethics committee approval and timely submission.
Perform and supervise cataract surgery, including phacoemulsification and manual small incision cataract surgery (MSICS), with documented outcomes and complication audits.
Manage general and subspeciality cases across glaucoma, retina, cornea, oculoplasty, paediatric ophthalmology, strabismus and neuro-ophthalmology, co-managing or referring as clinically appropriate.
Conduct outpatient clinics, inpatient rounds and ophthalmic emergency care, including ocular trauma, with accurate and complete clinical documentation.
Supervise and interpret ophthalmic diagnostics such as slit-lamp biomicroscopy, perimetry, optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus imaging, biometry and B-scan ultrasonography.
Initiate, conduct and publish original research in indexed journals, and pursue intramural and extramural research funding.
Design and conduct formative and summative assessments, and serve as internal or external examiner for university examinations as assigned.
Ensure departmental compliance with NMC Minimum Standard Requirements, faculty norms and documentation for NMC and university inspections.
Mentor and appraise junior faculty, senior residents, postgraduate residents and interns to support their academic and professional growth.
Contribute to community eye-care activities aligned with the National Programme for Control of Blindness and Visual Impairment (NPCBVI), including screening camps where organised.
Uphold patient safety, infection control, informed consent and quality standards, and participate in clinical audits, morbidity reviews and accreditation activities.
Participate in institutional committees, continuing medical education (CME) programmes and departmental planning, including equipment and service development.

Required Qualifications
MBBS from a recognised institution, with valid registration with the NMC or a State Medical Council, and registration with the State Medical Council of the work-location state as required by norms.
MS Ophthalmology, MD Ophthalmology or DNB Ophthalmology recognised by the NMC; DNB holders must meet NMC equivalence conditions for teaching appointments. A Diploma in Ophthalmology (DO) alone does not qualify for this position.
Eligibility for the post of Professor under the prevailing NMC Teachers Eligibility Qualifications (TEQ) regulations, including at least 3 years as Associate Professor in Ophthalmology in an NMC-recognised or permitted medical college.
At least four research publications in indexed journals (PubMed/Medline, Scopus, Embase, Science Citation Index or DOAJ) as first, second, third or corresponding author, with at least two published as Associate Professor, as per NMC criteria.
Completion of the Basic Course in Biomedical Research (BCBR) and the Basic Course in Medical Education (BCME), as required by the NMC.

Required Experience
Experience range: 820 years of post-PG teaching experience in Ophthalmology in NMC-recognised or permitted medical colleges. Minimum: 8 years of post-PG teaching experience, including at least 3 years as Associate Professor in Ophthalmology. Preferred: 12–20 years combining teaching, high-volume surgical practice and postgraduate thesis guidance; experience as Professor or Head of Department is an advantage. Relevant experience includes faculty roles (Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Professor) in medical colleges and university teaching hospitals; senior consultant service in NBEMS-accredited teaching departments of government institutions counts only where it meets NMC equivalence norms.

Technical and Functional Skills
Cataract surgery: phacoemulsification and MSICS, including complicated cataracts and management of intraoperative complications.
Glaucoma: gonioscopy, perimetry interpretation, trabeculectomy and laser procedures such as YAG peripheral iridotomy.
Retina: diabetic retinopathy and retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) screening, retinal laser photocoagulation and intravitreal injections.
Cornea and oculoplasty: infective keratitis and ocular surface disease, familiarity with keratoplasty, and lid, lacrimal (such as DCR) and ocular trauma procedures.
Diagnostics and other: paediatric, strabismus and neuro-ophthalmology evaluation; OCT, fundus photography, automated perimetry, biometry, B-scan ultrasonography and corneal topography.
Medical education: CBME delivery, competency-based assessment, logbook supervision, and skills-lab and wet-lab teaching.
Research: study design, biostatistics, ethics committee processes, Good Clinical Practice and scientific writing.
Regulatory: NMC Minimum Standard Requirements, TEQ regulations, inspection documentation and NPCBVI norms.

Soft Skills and Behavioural Competencies
Academic leadership and the ability to build a cohesive, high-performing teaching department.
Clear, compassionate communication with patients, families and multidisciplinary teams.
Mentorship and constructive feedback for students, residents and junior faculty.
Ethical judgement, professionalism and sound decision-making in surgical and emergency settings.
Collaboration with other departments, administration and research teams, and effective time management across clinical, teaching and research duties.

Preferred or Value-Added Qualifications
Subspeciality fellowship (glaucoma, vitreoretina, cornea, oculoplasty or paediatric ophthalmology) from a reputed eye institute.
Prior experience as Head of Department or as a university-recognised postgraduate guide.
Advanced Course in Medical Education (ACME), Curriculum Implementation Support Program (CISP) training or a recognised medical education fellowship.
Funded research as principal or co-investigator, publications beyond the NMC minimum, and peer-review or editorial roles.
Experience preparing departments for NMC or university inspections, and membership of professional bodies such as the All India Ophthalmological Society (AIOS).

Professional Tenure and Background
The ideal candidate will show a progressive academic career from Senior Resident to Assistant Professor, Associate Professor and Professor (or eligibility for Professor) in Ophthalmology, with stable tenures in NMC-recognised medical colleges, university teaching hospitals or reputed tertiary eye-care institutes. Candidates from government, deemed-university and established private medical colleges with active postgraduate programmes are well suited. A consistent record of surgical volume, documented publications and postgraduate guidance is expected, and career gaps or frequent short tenures should be explained in the application.

Compensation and Benefits
The compensation package is competitive and commensurate with qualifications, academic seniority and experience, in line with norms for senior medical faculty. Benefits are as per institutional policy, within an academic environment that supports teaching, research and professional growth. Compensation details will be discussed with shortlisted candidates.

Application Instructions
Send an updated CV mentioning the role "Professor – Ophthalmology" to careers@execvera.com, or by LinkedIn message or WhatsApp message to 9071197415. The CV should list qualifications with year and institution, NMC or State Medical Council registration number, designation-wise teaching experience with dates, indexed publications with author position, BCBR and BCME completion, annual surgical volumes, theses guided, current and expected annual CTC in , and notice period in days. Shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next steps.

Ensure smooth academic operations, timetabling, and compliance

Description:
Role Overview
The Librarian will be responsible for the overall management, development, digitisation, and effective utilisation of the University Library and its learning resources. The role goes beyond the traditional management of books and circulation. The Librarian is expected to develop the library as a student-centric Learning Resource Centre that actively supports teaching, research, skill development, employability, innovation, and lifelong learning. The Librarian will ensure that physical and digital resources are easily accessible, appropriately organised, effectively utilised, and continuously aligned with the academic programmes and evolving requirements of Medhavi Skills University.
Key Responsibilities
A. Library Administration & Operations
Manage the day-to-day functioning of the University Library and associated learning/resource facilities.
Develop and implement library policies, SOPs, circulation procedures, membership norms, and operating guidelines.
Ensure systematic acquisition, accessioning, classification, cataloguing, shelving, circulation, and preservation of library resources.
Maintain accurate records of books, journals, periodicals, newspapers, reports, reference materials, and other resources.
Ensure efficient issue, return, renewal, reservation, and recovery of library materials.
Conduct periodic stock verification and reconciliation of library resources.
Maintain appropriate systems for damaged, lost, obsolete, and withdrawn materials.
Ensure appropriate library timings based on student s and academic requirements, including during examinations and other high-demand periods.
B. Digital Library & Technology
Develop and strengthen the University s digital library ecosystem.
Manage e-books, e-journals, research databases, institutional repositories, online learning resources, and other digital subscriptions.
Ensure effective implementation and utilisation of the Library Management System (LMS/ILMS).
Facilitate remote and campus-based access to digital learning resources wherever applicable.
Promote awareness and usage of digital databases and online academic resources among students and faculty.
Explore emerging technologies, including AI-enabled search, research and knowledge management tools, to enhance library services.
Maintain accurate digital catalogues and ensure easy discoverability of resources.
C. Academic & Student Support
Work closely with Heads of Schools, Programme In-Charges, faculty members, and academic teams to understand programme-specific resource requirements.
Ensure availability of textbooks, reference books, journals, case studies, reports, and digital resources required for different programmes.
Conduct library orientation programmes for newly admitted students.
Train students in effective use of catalogues, databases, e-resources, research platforms, and credible online information sources.
Support students in literature searches, assignments, projects, presentations, research, and academic referencing.
Develop initiatives to improve reading habits and library utilisation among students.
Organise book displays, reading campaigns, author interactions, knowledge sessions, quizzes, book reviews, and other library engagement activities.
D. Faculty & Research Support
Assist faculty and researchers in identifying relevant books, journals, databases, reports, and research materials.
Support literature review, reference management, citation practices, and information retrieval.
Facilitate awareness of research databases, open-access resources, institutional repositories, and scholarly publications.
Support the development and maintenance of an institutional repository for research papers, publications, reports, projects, dissertations, and other academic outputs, as applicable.
Coordinate with academic teams for continuous improvement of programme-wise library resources.
E. Acquisition & Resource Development
Prepare annual and periodic plans for acquisition of books, journals, databases, and other learning resources.
Collect recommendations from faculty, Schools, and academic departments.
Evaluate resource requirements based on curriculum, student strength, programme requirements, usage patterns, and applicable regulatory norms.
Coordinate with publishers, vendors, distributors, and service providers for procurement and subscriptions.
Support comparative evaluation and cost-effective procurement of library resources in accordance with University policies.
Monitor subscriptions and ensure timely renewal of essential databases, journals, magazines, and digital resources
F. Compliance, Accreditation & Documentation
Maintain all library documentation required for statutory, regulatory, accreditation, audit and quality-assurance purposes.
Support the University in documentation and data requirements relating to UGC,

Description:
Program Associate - District Coordination

Position Overview
The Program Associate will provide strategic and operational support to the District Administration, ensuring effective coordination and convergence among relevant departments across the assigned district and blocks.

Roles and Responsibilities
Conduct situational assessments and district-level gap analyses to identify challenges in child protection.
Undertake vulnerability mapping and facilitate the linkage of vulnerable children and families with appropriate central and state government welfare schemes.
Strengthen the functioning of child protection systems and institutions.
Support the protection and rehabilitation of children affected by child marriage, child trafficking, child labour, and other forms of exploitation.
Assist the District Administration in inspecting child protection institutions and schools to ensure compliance with applicable laws, standards, and safeguarding protocols.
Organize capacity-building workshops for government officials, frontline workers, and relevant stakeholders.
Conduct awareness and sensitization workshops at district and block levels on child protection issues, including child marriage, child labour, child trafficking, and child sexual abuse.
Facilitate interdepartmental coordination and convergence among stakeholders working on child protection.
Track progress on key indicators related to education, health, nutrition, and child protection to support timely corrective action.
Support data-driven planning, monitoring, and decision-making processes.
Document key learnings, insights, and best practices to improve programme implementation and outcomes.

Education and Experience
Graduate with 1 to 2 years of relevant work experience; or
Postgraduate/Masters degree with up to 1 year of relevant work experience.

Required Skills
Strong commitment to child protection and welfare initiatives.
Good communication and coordination skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships with stakeholders.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple responsibilities.
Analytical thinking and practical problem-solving abilities.
Fluency in the local language(s) spoken in the assigned community will be preferred.

Leadership skills and the ability to motivate and manage a team effectively.

Description:
Job Summary
ATREE is seeking an Analyst to work closely with the Policy Lead to review, analyses, study, conduct consultations, and draft recommendations on mountain-specific policies related to biodiversity conservation, landscape restoration, and bio-resource use in the project landscapes and States.
You will be a key member of a team led by the Director -The Himalaya Initiative. You will represent ATREE to external stakeholders, including government departments in the project states, IHR states, and at the national level, and will collaborate closely with regional teams in the IHR and at ATREE headquarters in Bengaluru.
Responsibilities
Support the Policy Lead in delivering the policy component of the AMP-Himalaya project, including timely reporting and tracking of success indicators.
Review rangeland, forest, and agroforestry policies and identify opportunities to strengthen mountain-specific approaches across the three landscapes.
Support development and advocacy of state-level policy action plans on restoration and agroecology (Sikkim), OECM/CCA (Arunachal Pradesh), and rangeland and pastoral governance (Ladakh).
Support the Policy Lead in mapping key stakeholders in policy-making and comparing existing policies to identify gaps, overlaps, and mountain-specific needs across the three landscapes, keeping the analysis current.
Conduct FGDs, expert interviews, and workshops on mountain-specific policies, following FPIC and inclusive community-engagement protocols and supporting equitable participation of women and marginalized groups.
Identify practices or policies detrimental to climate and ecosystem resilience, and develop case studies of successful mountain-specific models or practices.
Support drafting of policy recommendations and briefing papers, and their presentation to a multi-stakeholder panel for review and feedback, delivered on schedule to support the Policy Lead.
Support the advocacy campaign to raise awareness and capacity strengthening activities, including training government officials, policymakers, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders.
Be part of the team compiling a comprehensive report and toolkit documenting the process, findings, recommendations, and outcomes for the IHR, and share it with stakeholders.
Support the team in creating the Legal-Institutional Framework and Modules for OECMs/CCA in Arunachal Pradesh, under the guidance of the Policy Lead and external legal counsel where required.
Support collaboration with ATREE s Academy for Conservation Science and Sustainability Studies and contribute to the project s digital knowledge commons, helping capture and curate policy-relevant data, analysis and case studies.
Write reports and support in contributing to the learning and reporting plan, and in coordinating with landscape, thematic, research, MEL and communications teams.
Represent ATREE in national and international forums and apply a proactive, strategic approach within and outside ATREE to deliver measurable policy impact.
Qualifications
Masters in a related field, i.e., environmental science, social sciences, natural science, ecology, natural resources management, public policy, law, or a related interdisciplinary field.
Experience Required
1 to 2 years of overall experience in policy work, with some experience in the mountains.
Strong networking skills and ability to build and maintain relationships with stakeholders.
Strong understanding of policy processes in government systems.
Understanding of, and commitment to, Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) and ethical community engagement protocols when working with indigenous and local communities in the IHR.
Sensitivity to gender and social inclusion considerations, with the ability to support equitable participation of women and marginalized groups in FGDs, consultations and workshops.
Excellent written and verbal English skills; knowledge of Hindi and/or a Himalayan regional language is an advantage; where not proficient, willingness to work through local translators/facilitators is required.
Proficient in analytical skills, report writing, and documentation.
Willingness to travel extensively across project locations in the Himalaya.
Skills to organize and communicate across levels of an organization and across geographies.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to work closely with team members.
Desirable Skills
Familiarity with data collection, coding, and analysis tools (e.g., Excel, Kobo Toolbox, or similar) for organizing consultation and FGD findings.
Prior exposure to national or regional mountain/biodiversity policy frameworks (e.g., National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem, State Biodiversity Action Plans) gained through coursework, internships, or prior roles.
Comfort with digital documentation and knowledge-management platforms for curating and organizing policy-relevant data and case studies.

Description:
Job Summary
Lead - Policy
ATREE is seeking an experienced professional to lead reviews, analyses, studies, consultations, and recommendations on mountain-specific policies related to biodiversity conservation, landscape restoration, and bio-resource use in the project landscapes and States. The policy vision will be guided by global, regional, national, and state mountain policies from IHR.
You will be a key member of a versatile team led by the Director - The Himalaya Initiative. You will represent ATREE with external stakeholders, including government departments in the project states, IHR states, and at the national level, and will collaborate closely with regional teams in the IHR and at ATREE headquarters in Bengaluru.
In the Himalaya, ATREE s strategy is to work towards a future where resilient mountain and downstream societies sustainably enjoy the natural endowment of the Indian Himalayan Region (IHR) while protecting and preserving its rich biodiversity. ATREE has developed a 10-year strategy called The Himalaya Initiative (THI), focused on the IHR amid increasing biodiversity loss, environmental degradation, and climate change.
Project AMP-Himalaya is funded by the Rural India Supporting Trust (RIST), co-financed by Conservation International and Global Conservation, within the THI strategy, for a 5-year project period. The project aims to conserve biodiversity, restore landscapes, and foster human well-being in the Indian Himalayan Region. Three key areas prioritized to achieve the goal in the IHR are: 1) Assessment, Monitoring, and Conservation of Biodiversity; 2) Restoration of Multi-functional Landscapes; and 3) Nature-based Rural Livelihoods and Climate Change Resilience. Integral to these priorities are: creating digital knowledge commons to accelerate participatory management and local stewardship; strengthening human resources through training programs for local youth leaders and expanded environmental education opportunities; and creating conditions to develop and implement multi-level, mountain-specific policies that prioritize biodiversity conservation and natural resource management at scale.
The project is being implemented in 3 distinct landscapes located in 3 states and 1 union territory of IHR, namely: the Khangchendzonga Landscape covering the Darjeeling hills of North Bengal and Sikkim state; the Trans-Himalayan Landscape representing a high dependence on rangelands with agro-pastoral and pastoral systems in Ladakh; and Arunachal Pradesh with the largest, greenest, ethnically diverse and most biodiversity-rich landscapes.
Responsibilities
Develop and lead the roadmap and strategy, in collaboration with the THI Director, for the policy component of the AMP-Himalaya project, including annual workplans, timely donor and project reporting, and tracking policy outcomes and success indicators.
Lead and drive the process of reviewing existing policies related to biodiversity, forests, rangelands, agroforestry, restoration, bioresource use, nature-based livelihoods, and climate resilience, including stakeholder mapping to identify gaps, overlaps, and mountain-specific policy approaches across the three project landscapes.
Develop and advocate state-level policy action plans across all three landscapes, restoration and agro-ecology (Sikkim), OECM and CCA (Arunachal Pradesh), and rangeland and pastoral governance (Trans-Himalaya, Ladakh), ensuring balanced policy engagement across landscapes.
Lead in conducting FGDs, expert interviews, and multi-stakeholder workshops, following FPIC and inclusive community-engagement protocols and ensuring equitable participation of women and marginalized groups; use findings to flag policies/practices harmful to climate and ecosystem resilience and document successful mountain-specific case studies.
Develop and lead a roadmap for presentation of policy recommendations and briefing papers for key stakeholders for validation, and compile a comprehensive IHR policy report and toolkit for dissemination to stakeholders.
Create and lead the development of Legal-Institutional Framework and Modules for OECM/CCA in Arunachal Pradesh, partnering with external legal counsel engaged by ATREE for specialized legal drafting where required.
Develop and lead policy engagement and advocacy campaigns to raise awareness and strengthen capacity, including training government officials, policymakers, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders.
Collaborate with ATREE s Academy for Conservation Science and Sustainability Studies and the project s digital knowledge commons to align policy work with ongoing research, fellowships and knowledge generation.
Contribute to the learning and reporting plan; provide technical guidance to Policy Analysts and Consultants; coordinate with landscape, thematic, research, MEL and communications teams.
Represent ATREE in national and international forums and apply a proactive, strategic approach within and outside ATREE to deliver measurable policy impact.
Qualifications
PhD in a related field, i.e., social sciences, environmental/natural sciences/natural resources management, public policy, law, economics, or a related interdisciplinary field.
A background in law, public policy, or economics is preferred in addition to the environmental/natural sciences; where specialized legal drafting is required (e.g., the Legal-Institutional Framework for OECMs/CCA), this will be carried out in partnership with external legal counsel engaged by ATREE.
Experience Required
5-6 years of professional experience in policy development and analysis, with substantial experience in mountain policy frameworks and a strong focus on the Himalaya.
Strong networking skills and demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with stakeholders.
Strong understanding of policy processes in government systems.
Demonstrated understanding of, and commitment to, Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) and ethical community engagement protocols when working with indigenous and local communities in the IHR.
Sensitivity to gender and social inclusion considerations, with the ability to help ensure equitable participation of women and marginalized groups in FGDs, consultations and workshops.
Excellent written and verbal English skills; knowledge of Hindi and/or a Himalayan regional language is an advantage; where not proficient, willingness to work through local translators/facilitators is required.
Excellent communication skills, with demonstrated ability to coordinate teams, motivate colleagues and engage effectively with diverse stakeholders.
Proficient in analytical skills, report writing, and documentation.
Willingness to travel extensively across project locations in the Himalaya.
Experience working with nonprofits in the Conservation / Environment / Sustainability / Biodiversity space highly desirable.
Self-motivated and able to work independently while collaborating across teams and geographies to deliver on a set of goals.
Strong organizational, interpersonal and leadership skills with the ability to motivate and lead small teams.
Desirable Skills
Working knowledge of international and regional mountain and biodiversity frameworks, including the CBD Global Biodiversity Framework, ICIMOD/Hindu Kush Himalaya frameworks, and UNFCCC/NDC processes.
Experience in grant management, resource mobilization, proposal writing, and donor engagement.
Experience using digital knowledge and communication tools, including data visualization and dashboards, to translate technical findings into accessible briefs and toolkits.

Role Overview:
Medhavi Skills University is seeking a dynamic Senior Manager Placements to lead the university s corporate engagement and student placement strategy at the Sikkim campus. This leadership role will be responsible for building strong industry partnerships, managing the placement team, and ensuring high-quality placement opportunities for students through strategic recruiter engagement. He will be responsible for getting all eligible
students placed.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Leadership & Team Management
Lead and manage the Campus Placement & Corporate Relations team to achieve placement goals.
Define KPIs, performance targets and accountability structures for the placement team.
Monitor team performance through regular reviews and ensure timely achievement of placement milestones.
Mentor team members and strengthen internal systems for effective placement management.
2. Industry Partnerships & Corporate Outreach for Placements
Develop and expand long-term partnerships with corporates, recruiters and industry bodies across sectors.
Identify and establish new recruitment partnerships for internships and final placements by frequent visits to Companies, Organizations PAN India.
Actively engage with industry leaders to position the university as a preferred talent sourcing partner.
Maintain strong relationships with existing recruiters to ensure recurring hiring engagements.
3. Placement Strategy & Performance Monitoring
Develop and implement the annual placement strategy for the campus.
Monitor placement progress across programs and ensure achievement of placement targets and quality benchmarks.
Establish systems for data-driven monitoring of placement performance, including placement dashboards and reports.
Provide periodic insights and updates to university leadership on placement outcomes.
4. Stakeholder Management
Work closely with academic leadership and faculty to align student skills with industry requirements.
Coordinate with internal teams to strengthen student employability and career readiness initiatives.
Ensure effective communication between students, recruiters, faculty, and the placement team.
5. Employer Branding & Institutional Representation
Represent the university in corporate meetings, industry forums, and networking platforms.
Promote the university s talent pool to attract high-quality recruiters and hiring partners.
Strengthen the university s reputation as an industry-aligned institution with strong placement outcomes.
Qualifications & Skills Required:
Master s degree in Management, HR or related field.
8-12 years of experience in placements, corporate relations or industry partnerships.
Mandatory: Prior experience managing placements in universities or higher education institutions at least 3-5 years.
Proven experience in building corporate partnerships and managing recruitment engagements.
Candidates should be proficient in: Corporate relationship management
Team leadership and performance monitoring
Strategic planning and execution
Stakeholder management
Strong networking and negotiation skills
Data-driven monitoring and reporting

What We Offer
Opportunity to architect and scale a future-focused, industry-integrated higher education ecosystem.
Competitive compensation with performance-linked incentives.
Leadership role in a rapidly growing national skills and university platform.
A collaborative, mission-driven environment.
The opportunity to create a measurable impact on employability and workforce transformation at scale.

Job Summary
A technical procurement specialist supports various business lines to identify, shortlist, select, and acquire suitable goods or services or works from a third-party vendor through a direct purchase while ensuring timely delivery of the right quality and quantity. This role is also expected to maintain and build relationships with the existing suppliers and strategically diversify NOV s supplier base through market research. Having technical aptitude, the technical procurement specialists ensure the conformance of goods and services with engineering specifications during the entire procurement process.
Primary Responsibilities
Work closely with the operations teams to understand procurement requirements details and request vendor quotes.
Participate in the new vendor approval process.
Capture technical and commercial information and order goods in correct quantities to maintain the supply and demand balance.
Coordinate with planning teams to gather service PO workscope, generate service POs and communicate information related to the scope and delivery terms with vendors.
Follow up with vendors and suppliers regarding goods and service procurement and update production teams about delivery date changes when vendor PO due dates are rescheduled
Identify and resolve issues with vendors arising throughout the procurement process.
Identify ongoing procurement process improvement opportunities, review with management and implement as directed.
Liaise with the account payable department.
Comply with local regulations, API and ISO standard requirements.
Participate in API and ISO audits and represent the NOV purchasing department.
Perform other work-related tasks as assigned.
Comply with all NOV Company and HSE procedures and policies.

Job Summary
The Builder - Logistics is a high-agency, 0-to-1 role embedded within Ca's GS Retail Logistics function in the South. Based out of Bengaluru and working closely with the Regional Head - South, you will build new programs, ship new tools, and run controlled experiments across Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, and Kerala. This is not a steady-state ops role - you'll spend most of your time defining problems, prototyping solutions, and turning what works into repeatable playbooks that city teams can run at scale. You'll operate at the intersection of ops, data, product, and AI.
Key Responsibilities
New Program Design - Identify gaps across pilot supply, CSP adherence, auto-allocation, and fulfilment. Design new programs from scratch, run pilots, and hand off winning plays to city teams.
Ops Diagnostics Deep Dives - Own regional data - cut it by city, cohort, and process step to surface what's broken and where the fastest wins sit. Convert findings into structured action plans.
Product Specs Tool Building - Write clear specs for internal tools and dashboards. Partner with Product and Tech to ship what the region needs; use no-code and AI where full builds are overkill.
Automation of Manual Workflows - Map the region's sheet-heavy workflows and lead their transition to automated systems. Ship quick wins with Apps Script, Zapier, or AI copilots before scoping full products.
City-Level Experimentation - Run controlled A/B tests across cities to validate whether a new process, script, or intervention actually moves the KPI. Kill what doesn't work, scale what does.
Cross-functional Execution - Work directly with city heads, Category Managers, Product, and Tech to unblock progress. Translate ground-team pain-points into shipped fixes fast.
Qualifications Experience
2-4 years in high-agency roles - startup ops, strategy consulting, category management, or founders office.
Track record of shipping something end-to-end - a program, a tool, a dashboard, a new city launch - that survived after you moved on.
Comfortable in ambiguity - can walk into a messy problem and leave with a structured plan.
Strong first-principles thinking; happy to visit yards and talk to pilots before writing a single line of a proposal.
Bengaluru-based or willing to relocate; comfortable travelling across Hyderabad, Chennai, and Kerala.
Data AI Skills
Advanced Excel / Google Sheets - pivots, lookups, and formula-based analysis at scale.
SQL fluency for querying large operational datasets; Python or R for deeper analysis is a strong plus.
Comfort building dashboards (Looker, Data Studio, Tableau) that drive city-level decisions.
Hands-on with AI copilots (ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or similar) to accelerate analysis, drafting, and prototyping.
Familiar with no-code automation (Apps Script, Zapier, Retool) to ship quick wins without engineering support.

#ACN Song GN Reinvention Services Customer Service Retail Service Reinvention Manager
Job Title Retail Service Reinvention Manager
Management Level: L07 Manager
Location: Bangalore, Gurgaon, Mumbai (India; global remit)
Experience: 10+ Years (L07)
Must have skills: Retail Service Reinvention / Customer Service Strategy Transformation; a blend of industry and consulting experience with deep understanding of the end-to-end retail value chain and how it drives service demand, volume and exceptions; experience shaping AI-native / agentic service operating models.
The Practice A Brief Sketch
The practice works with clients across their marketing, commerce, sales and service functions to reinvent how they engage customers. As part of the Reinvention Services Customer Service team, you will help the worlds leading retailers transform service from a reactive, cost-driven function into an intelligence-led, AI-native capability that senses signals in real time, resolves issues before they escalate, and continuously improves from every interaction across the shopper, store, supplier and fulfilment ecosystem driving customer value, growth, margin, operational efficiency and enterprise resilience.
Job summary
As a Retail Service Reinvention Senior Manager / Associate Director, you will advise C-suite executives, shape AI-native service operating models, and lead end-to-end transformation for the worlds leading retailers. Reporting to the Customer Service Managing Director, you will build and lead a team of Managers, Consultants and Analysts and carry accountability for generating business development opportunities upwards of USD 4M. The role requires a strong blend of retail domain expertise, consulting leadership, end-to-end value chain understanding, executive stakeholder management, and business development capability to shape and deliver scalable, future-ready retail service solutions.
Roles and responsibilities
Service Strategy Advisory
Define enterprise and omnichannel service strategy across the shopper, store, supplier and fulfilment ecosystems.
Shape AI-native service vision, target operating models and multi-year transformation roadmaps.
Develop business cases, prioritize investment and establish value-realization frameworks.
Advise boards and C-suite on where to sequence quick wins against enterprise-scale change.
Experience Design
Map end-to-end journeys for shoppers (order, delivery, returns, loyalty, complaints), associates (store, picker, contact centre) and suppliers (onboarding, purchase orders, invoicing, disputes).
Blueprint services across people, process, data and technology layers.
Identify moments of truth and design service recovery for stock-outs, failed deliveries, substitutions and disputed refunds.
Define channel strategy spanning mobile app, web, WhatsApp, voice, social, store desk and associate/picker devices.
Operating Model Process Transformation
Design target operating models spanning shopper services, supplier services, store workforce services, and fulfilment/ecosystem services.
Design the workforce across shoppers, store associates, pickers and inventory teams, contact-centre specialists and leads, supplier account teams, and delivery partners/dispatchers.
Establish governance frameworks policy and business rules, approval/escalation thresholds, SLAs and entitlements, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
Build KPI and performance frameworks tied to customer value, growth, margin, operational efficiency and enterprise resilience outcomes.
Technology AI Transformation
Set CRM and CCaaS platform strategy (Genesys, NICE, Salesforce Service Cloud, Five9, Amazon Connect).
Shape knowledge and case management (ServiceNow, Zendesk).
Design conversational and agentic AI (Kore.ai, Dialogflow) intent detection, content enrichment, knowledge graphs and decisioning/policy engines.
Integrate across order, store and supply-chain systems of record (OMS, POS, WMS, TMS, ERP, supplier/EDI portals) and IoT/GPS-enabled field and delivery tracking.
Build service analytics, predictive/prescriptive models and root-cause analysis capability.
Human + Agentic Operations
Design hybrid workforce models blending advisors, associates, AI copilots and autonomous agents across the shopper, supplier, store and fulfilment domains.
Design agents for high-volume service capabilities order status, substitutions, returns, refunds, delivery orchestration, supplier collaboration and dispute resolution.
Lead change management, upskilling and adoption programmes for frontline and support teams.
Establish AI governance, ethics and bias controls, and ongoing model/agent performance oversight.
Enterprise Transformation Delivery
Lead end-to-end programmes from strategy through implementation, adoption and value realisation.
Orchestrate multi-workstream delivery across business, experience, operations, technology and data/AI teams.
Manage executive steering committees and track value against committed business cases.
Practice Building
Develop market-leading thought leadership and intellectual property.
Build reusable methods, accelerators, assets and AI workflows for retail reinvention services.
Coach and mentor consulting teams.
Support business development and strategic pursuits collaborating with Song leadership to identify new opportunities and with Songs Consulting, Technology and Data AI teams for delivery.
Professional Technical Skills
Deep expertise in grocery, apparel or large omnichannel retail, with working knowledge of the end-to-end value chain merchandising and assortment planning, inventory and price management, promotions execution, digital commerce, in-store operations, supplier and partner operations, and last-mile fulfilment and how each stage drives customer demand, service volume and service exceptions.
First-hand practitioner experience inside leading grocery, apparel or omnichannel retailers (not advisory-only) having lived these operations, partnered with frontline teams, and redesigned them at enterprise scale.
Proven track record across service strategy advisory, experience design, operating model transformation, technology AI transformation, and enterprise delivery; consulting background is valuable but strong industry leadership experience counts equally.
Hands-on shopper/customer service experience across the lifecycle: order status and delivery-exception handling; substitutions, out-of-stock and refund/credit resolution; returns and reverse-logistics servicing; loyalty, rewards and membership servicing; complaint, feedback and social/review response; and multi-channel delivery (mobile app, web, WhatsApp, voice, social) with consistent resolution regardless of entry channel.
Supplier and partner service experience: onboarding, compliance and account management; forecast, purchase-order and inventory collaboration; quality issues, disputes and score-carding; invoice, payment and reconciliation servicing; and supplier/partner portals, EDI exchanges and account-management workflows.
Store and workforce service experience: inventory accuracy, price integrity and promotion execution at store level; pick, pack and in-store fulfilment; store-to-contact-centre escalation and case hand-off; associate empowerment tools (store apps, picker/associate devices, knowledge assistants); and workforce scheduling, service standards and frontline performance management.
Fulfilment and ecosystem service experience: delivery orchestration, routing and ETA/live tracking; failed-delivery, missed-slot and delivery-recovery workflows; reverse logistics and returns-to-warehouse operations; driver, dispatcher and 3PL partner management; and last-mile SLAs, on-time performance and partner score-carding.
Working knowledge of core retail service processes order-to-delivery, returns refunds, complaint case management, store-to-contact-centre escalation, substitution/refund workflows and supplier dispute resolution with the SLAs and benchmarks that define operational excellence, and fluency in how cases move end-to-end (detect, triage/categorise, route/assign, investigate/enrich, decide/approve, orchestrate, execute/communicate, confirm/close).
Exposure to the retail service technology and AI stack: CRM CCaaS (Genesys, NICE, Salesforce Service Cloud, Five9, Amazon Connect); knowledge case management (ServiceNow, Zendesk); conversational and agentic AI (Kore.ai, Dialogflow); systems of record (OMS, POS, WMS, TMS, ERP, PIM/MDM, pricing and promotions engines); supplier/EDI portals and IoT/GPS-enabled tracking; and the underlying AI/ML stack (intent detection, content enrichment, knowledge graphs, policy/rules engines, predictive/prescriptive models, decisioning/optimisation and root-cause analytics).
Experience designing target operating models that combine human and AI/agentic capacity reusable service capability design, hybrid workforce design, and governance/guardrail frameworks (policy business rules, approvals escalation, human-in-the-loop controls, SLAs entitlements, privacy consent, security access, compliance audit, model/agent performance governance, ethics bias controls, and data quality traceability).
Demonstrated track record of driving measurable outcomes customer value (NPS/CSAT, trust, advocacy); growth (repeat purchase rate, average order value, attach rate, customer lifetime value); service quality productivity (first-contact and overall resolution, reduced cost-to-serve and contact volume, higher associate productivity); and availability resilience (in-stock rate, on-time delivery/payment, margin protection, and supply/compliance resilience).
Executive stakeholder management, communication and storytelling; ability to build and defend a business case at board level; fluency across business, experience, operations, technology and AI/data teams; and comfort translating complex operating models into a clear enterprise narrative.
Additional information
Experience in retail, customer service or enterprise service transformation, including large-scale programmes delivered end-to-end from strategy through implementation; the ideal candidate blends industry and consulting experience.
Reports to the Customer Service Managing Director; builds and leads a team of Managers, Consultants and Analysts, with accountability for generating business development opportunities upwards of USD 4M.
Employment type: Permanent. Work arrangement: remote / hybrid / onsite, flexed to client and project needs; travel expectation varies by client engagement.
MBA or postgraduate qualification in retail preferred. Relevant certifications a plus CCXP, Six Sigma/Lean, ITIL, PMP, CSCP/APICS, Agile or Design Thinking, or platform certifications (Genesys, NICE, Salesforce).



Qualification
Experience in Retail industry (physical + digital) - Grocery, Apparel or large omnichannel retail sector experience
Good to have skills: relevant certifications (CCXP, Six Sigma/Lean, ITIL, PMP, CSCP/APICS, Agile or Design Thinking) and platform certifications (Genesys, NICE, Salesforce).
Educational Qualification: MBA or postgraduate qualification in retail preferred; MBA or equivalent degree in Business, Strategy, Sales Marketing.

Key Responsibilities
1. Databricks Enterprise Strategy
Define and own the enterprise-wide Databricks platform strategy, roadmap, and adoption model in line with business goals.
Set up a Databricks Center of Excellence (CoE), including best practices, reusable frameworks, and engineering standards.
Assess new Databricks capabilities (Unity Catalog, Delta Live Tables, Serverless, Photon, Mosaic AI, Databricks SQL) and lead their adoption.
Drive platform cost optimization (FinOps), workspace strategy, and capacity planning.
Act as the primary technical liaison with Databricks and cloud vendor partners.
2. Advanced DABs (Databricks Asset Bundles) Framework
Design and implement an enterprise-grade CI/CD framework using Databricks Asset Bundles for consistent, repeatable deployments.
Standardize Infrastructure-as-Code and Configuration-as-Code practices across environments (Dev, QA, UAT, Prod).
Integrate DABs with DevOps tools such as Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and Terraform.
Build reusable bundle templates, deployment patterns, and automated testing and validation pipelines.
Ensure version control, environment promotion, and release governance across all Databricks workloads.
3. Governance Implementation
Lead the design and rollout of data governance using Unity Catalog, covering access controls, data lineage, auditing, and data discovery.
Implement data security, privacy, and compliance controls (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2, CCPA, as applicable).
Define data quality frameworks, metadata management standards, and data ownership and stewardship models.
Work with InfoSec, Risk, and Compliance teams to enforce policies such as row/column-level security, data masking, and fine-grained permissions.
Set up monitoring, observability, and audit mechanisms across the data platform.
4. Data Lakehouse Architecture
Architect and evolve the enterprise Data Lakehouse using Delta Lake and the Medallion Architecture (Bronze, Silver, Gold).
Design scalable data models that support analytics, BI, ML/AI, and real-time use cases.
Lead migrations from legacy data warehouses, Hadoop, and on-prem platforms to the Databricks Lakehouse.
Ensure performance tuning, storage optimization (Z-Ordering, Liquid Clustering, partitioning), and high availability.
Enable data sharing through Delta Sharing and support data mesh and data product approaches where relevant.
5. Cloud Architecture (AWS / Azure)
Design secure, scalable, and resilient cloud-native data architectures on AWS and/or Azure.
Oversee the integration of Databricks with cloud services, such as:
Azure: ADLS Gen2, Azure Data Factory, Event Hubs, Key Vault, Synapse, Entra ID, Purview
AWS: S3, Glue, Kinesis, Lambda, IAM, Redshift, Lake Formation
Define networking, identity, and security architecture, including VNet/VPC injection, Private Link, and SSO/SCIM.
Drive disaster recovery, business continuity, and multi-region strategies.
6. Enterprise Data Pipeline Design
Lead the design and delivery of robust batch and streaming pipelines using PySpark, Spark SQL, Structured Streaming, Delta Live Tables, and Auto Loader.
Establish reusable ingestion, transformation, and orchestration frameworks (Databricks Workflows, Airflow, ADF).
Ensure pipelines meet SLAs, scalability, reliability, and data quality requirements.
Promote engineering excellence through code reviews, testing standards, modular design, and documentation.
Enable real-time and near-real-time data processing for critical business use cases.
7. Portfolio Management
Manage a portfolio of data engineering programs and projects, ensuring delivery on scope, schedule, budget, and quality.
Prioritize initiatives based on business value, ROI, and strategic alignment.
Own resource planning, budgeting, vendor management, and risk mitigation across the portfolio.
Report progress, KPIs, and outcomes to senior leadership and executive stakeholders.
Run delivery governance using Agile, SAFe, or hybrid methodologies.
People Leadership
Lead, mentor, and grow a team of data engineers, architects, and tech leads, including onshore and offshore teams.
Build a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous learning.
Drive hiring, performance management, and career development for the team.

Familiarity with Hugging Face Transformers, PEFT, TRL, Axolotl, or Unsloth.

Proficiency with LangGraph, LCEL, custom tools, retrievers, memory modules, and callbacks.

Ability to extend frameworks with custom components when needed.

Experience integrating and orchestrating multiple LLM providers and open-source models.
Ability to implement model routing, fallback mechanisms, load balancing, and cost optimization.
Exposure to multimodal models (text, image, audio, vision-language).
Familiarity with gateways and abstraction tools such as LiteLLM, OpenRouter, or similar.

Proven experience deploying LLM applications to production at scale.
Proficiency with model serving frameworks such as vLLM, TGI, Ollama, Triton, or TensorRT-LLM.
Strong knowledge of Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including services like Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI.
Experience with LLMOps and observability tools such as LangSmith, MLflow, Weights & Biases, Langfuse, or Arize.
Understanding of caching, batching, quantization, rate limiting, and latency optimization.

3+ years of people management experience leading, coaching, and developing teams of 6-7 or more direct reports.
Experience supporting multiple business units, product portfolios, or matrixed commercial organisations.
Knowledge of account development, market expansion, customer engagement strategies, and data-driven sales performance management across diverse geographic regions.
